label: People sharing for a property to be a boarding house
context: Tenancy Services says a property where six or more people share the accommodation by renting a room or a sleeping area, and share facilities such as the kitchen, bathroom or laundry, is probably a boarding house under the Residential Tenancies Act 1986.

label: Maximum bond
context: The most a boarding house landlord can ask for as a bond, as a number of weeks' rent. A bond above 1 week's rent must be lodged with Tenancy Services.

label: Time to lodge a bond over one week's rent
context: A boarding house landlord must lodge a bond of more than 1 week's rent with Tenancy Services within this many working days of receiving it, and give the tenant a receipt.

label: Most rent in advance
context: A landlord can ask for 1 or 2 weeks' rent in advance during the tenancy. Asking for more than 2 weeks' rent in advance is unlawful.

label: Notice of a rent increase
context: The least written notice a boarding house landlord must give before increasing the rent.

label: Minimum time between rent increases
context: Rent can be increased only once every 12 months, and not less than 12 months from the start of the tenancy.

label: Notice of a change to house rules
context: The least written notice a landlord must give tenants of a change to the house rules before it takes effect.

label: Penalty for not meeting the healthy homes standards
context: A boarding house that does not meet the healthy homes standards when it is required to may be liable for this penalty. Landlords must also include a healthy homes standards compliance statement in a new or renewed boarding house tenancy agreement.

label: Notice to inspect a room
context: The least notice a landlord must give to inspect a tenant's room. Inspections must be between 8am and 6pm unless the tenant and landlord agree another time.

label: Most frequent room inspections
context: A landlord can inspect a room no more than once in this many weeks.

label: Notice a tenant gives to end the tenancy
context: A boarding house tenant can end the tenancy with this much notice. It does not have to be in writing, though putting it in writing is a good idea.

label: Notice a landlord gives to end the tenancy
context: A boarding house landlord normally needs to give this much written notice. There are exceptions for serious damage, danger or disruption, overdue rent, illegal use and abandoned rooms.
